review.summary: Phase 90 is now a solid, honestly-evidenced plan gate, and every blocking finding from attempt-01 is genuinely fixed in the reviewed source — not just claimed. I verified each fix by reading the code: the publication record is selected by the entry that carries `registry_publication` instead of `phases[-1]` (tools/test_ci.py:213-216), empty/missing unittest discovery now fails closed before the subprocess runs (tools/check_phase.py:23-31, 37-39) with both a reject and an accept unit test (tools/test_review_phase.py:25-41), the maintenance successor is the smallest greater phase id (tools/review_phase.py:156-158) with 8→90→91 coverage (tools/test_review_phase.py:19-23), how active_phase 90 was established is recorded (docs/phase-status.json:1810-1813), and the phase-90 gate was widened to the pinned-commit whitespace range, the 26-test CI governance suite and a fresh private-material scan (tools/check_phase.py:71-80). The attempt-01 documentation conflicts are resolved coherently: docs/RELEASE.md:24-28 routes 0.1.1 through gates 90/91, RELEASE.md:83-85 and docs/implementation-plan.md:127 document the authorized external mode-0600 token until trusted publishing exists, and the plan now records exact publish/verify commands, receipt paths and a download-and-compare publication verifier (docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:125-175) rather than treating CLI success or a tag as proof. Check evidence is tight and actually executed: docs/checks/phase-90.json lists exactly the seven commands of commands_for(90) in order, all with integer exit_code 0 and timeout false, bound to source_sha256 ed8f9529 with source_unchanged true, and the private-material receipt it validates was itself produced against that same fingerprint and HEAD a6d63e5 with zero credential/tenant matches (docs/checks/phase-90-private-material.json:3-16), with check_receipt enforcing passed/sourceUnchanged/zero-match structure and recomputing the source fingerprint (scripts/check-private-material.py:155-176). The compatibility contract matches the pinned code: Mode stays #[non_exhaustive] with the additive variant (validation.rs:13-37), RequestOptions::with_timeout is the only constructor and sets response_defaults: true (config.rs:368-381), request validation is untouched, absent defaults are still walked and validated before suppression (validation.rs:525-530, 764-771), and response_mode()'s cfg gate (config.rs:414-430) exactly matches the gates on decode_contract/send_contract_one_of and the gateway-only ContractStream, so no feature combination is left uncompilable by inspection. It falls short of 9 on one medium: the phase-91 acceptance command set that this phase exists to define (tools/check_phase.py:81-108) is materially narrower than the 0.1.0 release gate for a change that touches the core validator and the SSE decode path — it drops cross-target compile checks for the three non-host targets docs/PLATFORMS.md:11-13 still advertises, tracing stress, native fixture/oracle verification and the stronger verify-contracts forms — and plan step 91.5 directs CI to replace the phase-8 invocation with it, removing those from CI too, with no disclosure of the narrowing or of the resulting evidence limitation. Supporting lows: the review-disposition ledger is incomplete for two attempt-01 lows, the unconditional acceptance-parity claim still ships in CHANGELOG.md:12, docs/VALIDATION.md:20-21 and a source comment at validation.rs:764-765 despite the recorded counterexample, phase-90 scope_evidence omits the tooling and documentation artifacts the phase actually changed, and the plan's claimed independent Standards/Spec reviews have no retained artifact. No high or blocker: I found no credential exposure, no gate-bypass path, and no compile-gating or propagation defect beyond the two defects the plan already books as phase-91 work.

findings.description: The phase-91 acceptance command set — the main artifact phase 90 is responsible for defining — is substantially narrower than the gate that qualified 0.1.0, for a change that modifies the core validator (validation.rs), public RequestOptions, the buffered contract decode path and the Gateway SSE contract path. Relative to commands_for(8) it omits: scripts/check-cross.py for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (tools/check_phase.py:252-254), scripts/check-tracing-stress.py (255-257), tools/verify_native_fixtures.py --require-test-bindings and the native-fixture/model-fixture suites (198, 236-238), the TypeScript extraction/oracle determinism checks inherited from commands_for(1) (115-120, 149-153), and the stronger `tools/verify-contracts.py --baseline .local/typescript` and `--self-test` forms (113-114) — the phase-90 run of the plain form reports extractedBaselineVerified false and excludedRemoteBytesVerified false (docs/checks/phase-90.json:132). Plan step 91.5 (docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:87-96) additionally directs CI to replace `check_phase.py --phase 8 --verification-only` (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:72) with the 91 gate, so those checks also leave CI; the 46-job rust matrix (ci.yml:89-90) covers isolated features but not cross-target compilation, cross-compile targets are dispatch-only (.forgejo/workflows/native-platforms.yml:4), and docs/PLATFORMS.md:11-13 keeps claiming compile-only support for the three non-host targets. Neither the plan nor docs/phase-status.json records this narrowing as deliberate or as a 0.1.1 evidence limitation.
findings.required_fix: Either extend commands_for(91) with scripts/check-cross.py for the four recorded targets, tools/verify_native_fixtures.py --require-test-bindings, the fixture/oracle determinism checks and the `--baseline .local/typescript`/`--self-test` verify-contracts forms (and keep or consciously drop check-tracing-stress.py), or enumerate in docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:87-96 exactly which phase-8 commands are deliberately not re-run for 0.1.1, record that exclusion in the phase-90/91 records in docs/phase-status.json, and state the resulting staleness of the docs/PLATFORMS.md:11-13 compile-only claims for the 0.1.1 source.

findings.description: The phase-90 review-disposition ledger is incomplete and structurally inconsistent with every other phase. `review_fixes` is a single object with `attempt_01_score` and a prose `changes` list, whereas phases 1-8 use a list of records carrying `source`, `status`, `scope` and `acceptance_evidence` per finding (for example lines 692-713). Two attempt-01 findings have no recorded disposition at all: the acceptance-parity overclaim (docs/reviews/phase-90-attempt-01.json:51-57) and the missing docs/STABILITY.md basis for patch versioning plus machine-readable recording of the additive API (65-71) — the latter is only partly covered by the planned sidecar. The preserved attempt-01 check report docs/checks/phase-90-attempt-01.json (source 94de2818) is retained on disk but referenced nowhere, unlike the phase-8 `preserved_checks` pattern. Phase 8 itself was previously faulted for exactly this kind of incomplete ledger (docs/phase-status.json:873).
findings.required_fix: Convert phase 90's `review_fixes` to the list-of-records shape used by other phases, with one entry per attempt-01 finding carrying its status and resolution/acceptance evidence (including explicit dispositions for the two lows above), and reference docs/checks/phase-90-attempt-01.json as the preserved attempt-01 check report.

findings.description: User-facing text and a source comment still assert unconditional acceptance parity while the plan books a live counterexample. CHANGELOG.md:12 says "Acceptance is identical to the default policy", docs/VALIDATION.md:20-21 says "the same documents are accepted and rejected", and crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:764-765 comments "acceptance never depends on whether defaults are materialized" — but at validation.rs:766-771 the key is charged through self.copy_text(key) only when the property is present or the mode inserts defaults, so a suppressed default's key bytes never count against max_copied_bytes and a document near that limit can be accepted under ResponseWithoutDefaults and rejected under Response. docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:55-58 records this honestly as an unfixed phase-91 item and step 91.1 (line 69-70) now gates the unconditional claim on the fix, so this is deferred rather than misrepresented, and nothing is published; the source comment is nevertheless a false invariant with no test pinning it.
findings.required_fix: Qualify the three claims now with the limit-accounting exception, or land the copy/work accounting fix before they ship, and add a public-boundary regression test that pins equal copy accounting between Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults at the max_copied_bytes boundary when the fix lands.

findings.description: Phase 90's `scope_evidence` names only the plan, the source branch and the pinned commit, but the phase actually changed eight tracked artifacts: tools/check_phase.py (the 90 and 91 command sets plus require_nonempty_tests), tools/review_phase.py (next_phase), tools/test_ci.py (publication lookup), tools/test_review_phase.py (new cases), docs/PHASES.md:19-24, docs/CI.md:10-12, docs/RELEASE.md:24-28/83-85 and docs/implementation-plan.md:127. A reader of the phase record cannot see the governance and documentation surface this phase modified, which is the same bookkeeping gap recorded against phase 8 at docs/phase-status.json:887-888.
findings.required_fix: List the actually changed tooling and documentation artifacts in phase 90's scope_evidence (or in milestones.implemented_scope.evidence when the phase is accepted), alongside the plan and pinned commit.

findings.description: The new pinned-commit whitespace check hardcodes `git diff --check 840c090..a6d63e5` and nothing asserts that HEAD still equals a6d63e5. The remaining two commands only inspect uncommitted and staged changes, so once phase 90's own bookkeeping (the plan, the status edits and the tooling changes currently uncommitted per git status) is committed, no phase-90 command covers that committed content, and a later commit on the branch would silently fall outside the fixed range. docs/checks/phase-90-private-material.json:5 does record headCommit a6d63e58, but check_receipt only validates that field's format (scripts/check-private-material.py:174-175), not that it equals the pin.
findings.required_fix: Use `840c090..HEAD` in commands_for(90), or add an assertion (in commands_for(90) or a governance unit test) that HEAD equals the pinned a6d63e5 and that the private-material receipt's headCommit matches the same pin.

findings.description: Phase 90 milestone 1 states "Independent Standards and Spec reviews supplement the actual Claude gate", but no such artifacts exist in the repository: docs/reviews/ contains only phase-90-attempt-01.json/.cli.json/.prompt.md and the attempt-02 prompt, and docs/phase-status.json's phase-90 record lists no evidence for them. The claim is therefore unverifiable from the reviewed source, in a phase whose entire deliverable is reviewed prose.
findings.required_fix: Retain the independent Standards and Spec review outputs under docs/reviews/ (or another recorded path) and reference them from the phase-90 record in docs/phase-status.json, or remove the claim from the plan.

findings.description: The scope section fixes the inputs but never states the basis for a patch release rather than 0.2.0, which docs/STABILITY.md supplies (patch releases stay source compatible; a variant on a #[non_exhaustive] enum plus two additive methods qualifies) — this was attempt-01's unaddressed low. The scope also does not require the 0.1.1 changelog to cover the full unpublished delta since the published 0.1.0 artifact: docs/phase-status.json:1780-1788 records the current workspace as an unreleased development snapshot whose packaged inputs already differ from the published 0.1.0 archive (changedPackagedInputs README.md), yet CHANGELOG.md:3-18 lists only the two API additions.
findings.required_fix: Cite docs/STABILITY.md's patch-compatibility rule in the plan's scope section as the stated basis for 0.1.1, and add a step requiring the dated 0.1.1 changelog entry to cover every packaged input that changed since the published 0.1.0 artifact, not only the new response-default API.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-90.json:7-154 records exactly the seven commands of tools/check_phase.py:71-80 in the same order (pinned-range whitespace, working-tree and staged whitespace, test_review_phase.py, test_ci.py, verify-contracts.py, private-material --check), every one with integer exit_code 0 and timeout false, bound to source_sha256 ed8f9529… with source_unchanged true and passed true; the stderr shows 28 review-gate tests and 26 CI governance tests OK.

Attempt-01's high is fixed and verified: tools/test_ci.py:213-216 now builds `publications` from every phase carrying `registry_publication` and asserts the last one, instead of indexing status["phases"][-1]; the phase-8 record still holds that key at docs/phase-status.json:1761 while phases 90 and 91 are appended after it, and the 26-test test_ci.py suite is now inside the phase-90 gate and recorded passing (docs/checks/phase-90.json:118).

Empty-suite hazard closed: tools/check_phase.py:23-31 discovers the suite and raises on countTestCases() == 0, and run_check:37-39 converts that into exit_code 1 before any subprocess starts, so the phase-91 slot for the not-yet-written tools/test_g10_release.py (tools/check_phase.py:86) can no longer record a vacuous pass; tools/test_review_phase.py:25-41 covers a missing file, an empty file and a populated suite.

Non-contiguous advancement is implemented and tested: tools/review_phase.py:156-158 returns min(number for number in phases if number > current), used at line 199, and tools/test_review_phase.py:19-23 asserts 8→90, 90→91 and None after 91; docs/phase-status.json:1810-1813 now records how active_phase 90 was established. The existence of docs/reviews/phase-90-attempt-01.prompt.md also proves validate_predecessors (review_phase.py:145-153) verified all eight predecessor review records against their accepted fingerprints before the prompt was written.

The private-material evidence is a real executed scan, not a stale receipt: docs/checks/phase-90-private-material.json:3-16 records checkedAt 12:58:13Z, sourceSha256 ed8f9529… (equal to the reviewed fingerprint), headCommit a6d63e58…, passed true, 1344 Git-visible files, 0 selected credential matches, 0 packaged-source matches and 0 new/changed tenant occurrences; scripts/check-private-material.py:155-176 rejects any receipt that is not a successful scan and recomputes both the source and packaged-candidate fingerprints, so the gate's `privateScanReexecuted: false` output is a freshness binding rather than an unexecuted check.

Compatibility contract confirmed in code: Mode is #[non_exhaustive] with the additive ResponseWithoutDefaults (crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:13-37); RequestOptions::with_timeout is the only constructor and sets response_defaults: true (crates/scm-sdk/src/config.rs:368-381); the additive methods are at config.rs:406-413; propagation is at engine.rs:643 (one-of), engine.rs:721 (buffered contract) and streaming.rs:113 (Gateway SSE), and validation.rs:525-530 still substitutes the schema default into the walk so an absent defaulted value is validated before being discarded at validation.rs:766-771.

Feature gating is self-consistent by inspection: config.rs:414-423 gates response_mode() on scan/management/gateway/dlp/iam/model-security/red-team/agentguard, which is exactly the gate on send_contract (engine.rs:598-607) and decode_contract (engine.rs:692-701); send_contract_one_of is gateway-only (engine.rs:621) and ContractStream — the only streaming caller — is #[cfg(feature = "gateway")] (streaming.rs:7-26), so the unconditional `pub mod streaming` does not expose the new call outside the gated set.

Documentation conflicts raised in attempt-01 are resolved: docs/RELEASE.md:24-28 states that the Phase 8 procedure below describes 0.1.0 and that its historical receipts do not qualify changed 0.1.1 inputs; docs/RELEASE.md:83-85 and docs/implementation-plan.md:127 document the authorized external mode-0600 Cargo token as an interim to trusted publishing with CI credential-free; docs/CI.md:10-12 records that the maintenance plan replaces the Phase 8 CI invocation together with the tools/test_ci.py expectations.

The release procedure is now concrete rather than prose: docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:139-152 lists the exact gate, review, commit, both --require-clean package proofs, tag, pushes, publish and verify-publication commands; lines 154-162 require the verifier to download the registry artifact and match owner cdot65, version, checksum, archive SHA-256, embedded commit, clean VCS metadata and file hashes, and explicitly state that neither a tag nor CLI success establishes the artifact; lines 164-170 fix the retained receipt paths; lines 126-132 forbid the token in arguments, repository configuration, output and receipts.

The plan's recorded defects are accurate and narrow, and the counted ledger checks out: contracts/native-semantics.json contains exactly 23 ZodDefault binding records (for example s000075 default 30 and s000080 default "days" from src/management/dashboard.ts, confirming product ownership outside Red Team), contracts/native-fixtures/schemas.json agrees, and the new test crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_resources_contracts.rs:2025-2120 exercises all seven target entry points plus both-mode rejection with operation name red_team.targets.get while consuming only one list_all page (10 queued replies, 10 asserted requests) and no explicit JSON null — exactly the limitation docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:55-58 books for phase 91.

The suppressed-default typed path is sound for the fields the docs cite: crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:8297-8298 and 12139-12140 type basic_auth_location and ws_response_timeout as Optional with serde default, so omission deserializes rather than failing, supporting the docs/VALIDATION.md:32-36 claim for those bindings; the general claim across all 23 bindings is not yet pinned by an executable check, which is what the planned contracts/response-defaults.json sidecar (docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md:99-101) is for.
limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep with no command execution: I could not recompute the reviewed fingerprint ed8f9529…, the docs/checks/phase-90.json digest, or the private-material receipt's recomputed fingerprints, and I could not run tools/test_ci.py or tools/test_review_phase.py. I verified the recorded exit codes, command equality against commands_for(90), and the fix logic by reading the code; the test results themselves are the gate's recorded evidence, not my own execution.

The phase-90 gate executes no Rust, generator, export, package, dependency or cross-compile check, so every runtime claim about the pinned branch (compilation under all 23 feature sets, clippy/rustfmt, the schema_contracts.rs corpus equivalence replay, the new red_team target test) is unexecuted evidence in this phase. My feature-gating and propagation conclusions are from source inspection only. This is the phase's declared scope (docs/PHASES.md:19, docs/phase-status.json:1808), not a concealed gap.

I sampled the 23 default bindings rather than exhaustively resolving each owning object, wrapper chain and generated Rust field type. I confirmed the two cited Red Team fields are Optional and that the dashboard bindings are request-side, but an effect- or refinement-observed acceptance difference elsewhere in the graph, and a non-Optional generated field for some defaulted response property, are not fully excluded; the plan's all-23 inventory and regression requirement remains the right control.

I could not run git, so I could not diff tools/check_phase.py, tools/review_phase.py, tools/test_ci.py, tools/test_review_phase.py, docs/CI.md, docs/RELEASE.md, docs/implementation-plan.md or docs/PHASES.md against their pre-phase state; I assessed them as current source. The pin 840c090..a6d63e5 rests on the commit subjects in the session context plus the headCommit recorded in docs/checks/phase-90-private-material.json:5.

I read no credential or tenant-registration material, nothing under .local/ except nothing at all, nothing outside this repository, and made no network calls. The plan's live-qualification, tag, push and crates.io steps are judged as written text; no part of them has been executed in this phase.
